correctness.rationale: Under the shared order sigma, the two forbidden nesting orientations are equivalent to the exact occurrence inequalities p(a,k-1)<p(b,1) and p(a,k)<p(b,2) for each pair ordered a before b. Adjacent inequalities enforce separation of every second block for \(k\ge3\), leaving exactly one optional last/first swap at each boundary. The \(k\ge3\) construction preserves all occurrence-rank orders, giving a bijection with (sigma,B). A swap increases descents by one and the major-index sum by k*i regardless of ascent/descent direction, verified by examining positions ki-1,ki,ki+1; these neighborhoods are disjoint for \(k\ge3\). The resulting product follows. The full finite exact-word verifier exhausts n<=4 k=3,4 and several larger cases, corroborating both normal form and bivariate coefficients.

value.rationale: The 2026 paper singles out the {1221,2112} canon class by its remarkable \(n!2^{n-1}\) count; that motivates asking for a substantive statistic refinement rather than a trivial arbitrary subclass. The exact Euler–Mahonian product is a complete joint descent/major-index classification with a natural boundary-position interpretation, positivity, palindromicity, and a sharp congruence/spectrum law for major index. A scalar count and even a full descent-only polynomial cannot recover its q coefficients. The theorem furnishes a reusable weight-preserving bijection for further refinements of restricted canon permutations, rather than an unmotivated isolated numeric calculation.
